test: still submits (photos/details are not privileged) when consent has not been accepted
evidence: Static source/caller review only. The denied flag in this case is the overall data-collection consent (`accepted=false`, `acceptedVersion=null`), not analytics consent (`analyticsAccepted` is not changed). `useConsentStore.ts:3-14` says photos/location/details transmission must gate on current overall consent and describes analytics as an additional, independent opt-in; `src/lib/analytics/analytics.ts:76` applies both gates to analytics. The case directly calls `useSubmissionSubmit` and asserts its mocked upload boundary is invoked, bypassing the ordinary route path: Home redirects unconsented users to intro-flow (`src/screens/home/index.tsx:100-114`), while Submission Details mounts the hook directly and has no visible consent guard (`src/screens/submission/create/index.tsx:60-62`). Thus it is a focused hook-boundary unit test, but it also deliberately asserts behavior contrary to the store contract. It is not evidence that an end-user can reach this state; no execution evidence was collected.
changes: None; read-only audit. Clarify whether this test is intended to verify an isolated submit-hook contract or to assert product policy for saved drafts after consent is withdrawn/versioned. It does not test analytics-consent independence.

verification.command: Static review of useConsentStore.ts, screens/home/index.tsx, screens/consent/index.tsx, and useSubmissionSubmit.ts

remaining_risk: Whether current overall consent is required again to transmit a previously saved draft is a product/policy question not resolved by the reachable Home flow. Direct route access may also be possible; no route-level guard is present in the inspected Submission Details screen.
flaw_details: Only if interpreted as a user workflow: it combines a fully ready draft with missing overall consent and directly invokes the hook, though the ordinary app route is gated upstream. It is an intentional isolated hook call, so this is uncertain rather than a confirmed unrealistic test.
